text:
Maria: FYI I ran the autoscale/burst-credit experiment on dedicated-west-2 this morning. High-level: p95 within SLA, but p99 spikes on cold nodes when KV misses and kernel fallback kicks in. Scale-up avg ~14s under sustained ramp; cold process startup ~3s plus ~600ms extra for kernel selection/JIT on first few requests. Posting quick notes below.

Jake: which harness did you use? replay or synthetic?

Maria: replay harness with synthetic overlay to stress different prefix distributions. Config: 
```
replayer: replay/2026-11-customerA.json
traffic-mix: 70% short (<64), 30% long (~512)
burst: 200 rps for 30s every 5m
warmup: none (intentional cold starts)
```

Ronit: curious — the p99 spikes correlate with KV misses? can you paste the short flame snippet?

Maria: yes. sequence: request hits uncached prefix -> KV cache miss -> runtime falls back to full KV reconstruction path -> kernel selection prefers default dense kernel (slow for quantized weights) -> 600-900ms extra. snippet: 
```
# p99 sample (ms)
latency: 1420
kv_miss_path: 860
kernel_jit: 120
context_load: 80
other: 360
```

Anna: hmm. two levers: 1) pre-warm KV cache for high burst tenants; 2) prefer quantized kernel when model is quantized even if not warmed. The latter avoids heavy JIT on cold.

Ben: I profiled with perf and async traces. The first request after node spin-up spent ~40% time in kernel selection heuristics (searching kernel table + loading kernel blobs). After 5 warm requests that drops to ~3%. So warm-up clearly helps.

Jake: are burst credits getting consumed fast? any dedicated pool config differences?

Maria: yep we depleted burst credits on one pool after 3 bursts (config 3x short bursts allowed). When credits hit 0, scale-up slowed because we waited for spare capacity in the reserved group -> extra ~6s.

Ronit: that's important. Proposal: change policy to allow transient overcommit on dedicated pools up to X for Y seconds if p99 > threshold. Then auto-evict non-SLA traffic.

Anna: another quick test idea: run replay but with an initial 10 warm requests per node to populate KV and trigger kernel JIT before opening the burst. Compare p99 and overall token cost.

Maria: did that in a side run: warm-10 reduced p99 from 1.42s -> 0.62s on cold wheels, and reduced extra kernel_jit cost to ~30ms. Token cost increased ~0.6% due to warm ops.

Ben: good data. Can we also compare kernel-selection policy A (prefer default fastest raw throughput) vs B (prefer kernel with fastest first-token latency) for apples-to-apples? I suspect B wins for PLG-facing short requests.

Jake: agreed. We should add a controlled AB with same load and seed randomness. Use replay harness with identical seeds and track p50/p95/p99 + cold-start tail.

ci-bot: test-run 1769123456-branch-autoscale-experiment complete. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/1769123456

Ronit: next steps: 1) run AB kernel policy for 2 hours across 2 pools, 2) implement transient overcommit config (#issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/489), 3) schedule a longer replay with mixed prefixes.

Maria: I'll kick off the AB later today and link results in the issue. Thanks all. :clap:

Anna: assigning follow-up sync on monday to discuss rollout if AB shows improvement.

Ben: adding perf traces to the issue.

Jake: nice work, Maria.
